title: Gasdermin E couples viral pyroptosis to lethal hepatic lipid accumulation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file exists to open. I checked: Europe PMC record (subscription-only, not in PubMed Central, hasSuppl=N); Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint (HTTP 404); NCBI elink from PubMed ID 42526439 to GEO, SRA, BioProject and BioSample (zero links in all four); GEO keyword searches for 'wetland virus', 'WELV', 'orthonairovirus' and taxonomy ID 3366332 (zero hits); PRIDE proteomics archive search (empty); Zenodo (0 hits) and figshare (no relevant hits); the publisher abstract page at cell.com returned HTTP 403. Only machine-found identifiers in the text are 25 RRID antibody catalogue numbers.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the science: that wetland virus (WELV, a tick-borne orthonairovirus) infection raises liver enzymes and triacylglycerol in patients, that gasdermin E (GSDME, a pore-forming cell-death protein) drives hepatocyte pyroptosis via RIG-I/caspase-3, that GSDME binds fatty acid synthase (FASN) and blocks its degradation, and that GSDME knockout mice survive. Patient numbers, mouse group sizes and any RNA-sequencing or lipidomics experiments are unknown to me because only the abstract is accessible.

a1_downloadable.note: No obtainable dataset. Article is subscription-only with no PubMed Central deposit, Europe PMC lists no supplementary files (404 from the supplementaryFiles endpoint), and there are no accessions in GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, PRIDE, Zenodo or figshare linked to PubMed ID 42526439. Publisher page blocked (HTTP 403). This is an A1 failure, verified by probing every repository rather than by reading the paper.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and moot: with no table there is no column. Any label (e.g. pyroptosis status, liver triacylglycerol level) would have to be constructed from figure panels.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature matrix of any kind is available; the only machine-readable identifiers in the record are 25 antibody RRIDs.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable — no data file. Abstract mentions hepatic enzymes and triacylglycerol but no values or units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Mechanistic virology study: a small patient cohort plus mouse and cell-line experiments. Even if figure-source data were released, the unit of analysis would be tens of animals or patients, far under the ~400-row floor. No count verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized because there is nothing to download.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: no download, no application programming interface record of file contents, and no full text to state counts against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not traceable. The outcomes (pyroptosis, steatosis, survival) are real lab measurements, but none are released in machine-readable form, so provenance cannot be checked at row level.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no machine-readable data, so there is nothing a model could be trained or tested on.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence to predict which host proteins caspase-3 cuts to trigger cell death during infection
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would have needed per-protein or per-site rows pairing sequence with a measured cleavage or pyroptosis readout; this paper provides zero such rows (verified: no supplementary files, no repository deposits).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a protein is cleaved by caspase-3 at a given site, with the truth coming from gel-based cleavage assays like those in this paper's figures — which are images, not tables.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Nothing can be learned from this paper's released data because none exists; the biology is interesting but the usable training labels for caspase cleavage live in older curated resources, not here.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The underlying biology (caspase-3 cleavage of gasdermin E and of the viral nucleoprotein) maps onto an existing, well-served task — sequence-based protease cleavage-site prediction, already addressed by DeepCleave (2020, Bioinformatics) and newer pan-protease models — but the labels for that task would come entirely from curated cleavage databases, not from this paper. This paper contributes no training data.

effort.compute_note: No estimates made because there is no dataset; all numbers left null rather than guessed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query NCBI elink from the PubMed ID to GEO/SRA/BioProject and the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint — both came back empty in under a minute, which kills the project immediately.

verdict_reason: Paywalled mechanistic virology paper with no downloadable data anywhere: no PubMed Central full text, no supplementary files, and zero deposits in GEO, SRA, BioProject, PRIDE, Zenodo or figshare. Part A1 fails outright, and the study design (small patient cohort plus mouse experiments) would also fail the row-count killer even if figure-source data appeared.
